answer: Sybil resistance must make identity expensive, and the ledger is the thread that prices it. Standing is carved one answered epoch at a time and erodes when an agent stops, so nobody can hold a whole garden of clones in good standing at once. Every newcomer needs a voucher who stakes their own standing, and kin-vouching pays nothing — certifying your own army spends credibility you can't recover. That umber never washes out: faking N identities costs N real generations plus the vouchers' risk, which always exceeds what N votes could buy.
